records.description: Present and preterite subjunctive each have one singular form for all3persons and one plural form for all3persons. Selected normal endings -e/-en; contracted/anomalous rows explicit. Full672cells+6bēo alternatives.

Use present stem without indicative2/3sg umlaut; use strong preterite plural stem in both subjunctive numbers. Weak past retains its dental stem. Present subjunctive preterite-presents use lexical plural-type/umlauted forms, not strong indicative singular.

Independent present subjunctive expresses wishes/exhortations, including thirdperson Let... and firstplural Letus.... Secondperson imperative and subjunctive are formally/syntactically distinct even where spellings coincide. English let here is not a new lǣtan causative construction.

Open gif clauses can use indicative. A contextually tentative/hypothetical request can use present subjunctive, followed by an imperative or ordinary indicative main clause. Gif itself never licenses an automatic conversion rule.
With explicit unreal/nonpast context and supplied interpretation, preterite subjunctive can refer to nonpast events. No rigid unscaffolded English would template or all counterfactual types assigned.

Keep learned mæg capability, mōt permission, wille/wolde volition distinct from inflectional subjunctive wishes. A past spelling does not mechanically mean English would/might; willan is not automatically future. Preserve bounded earlier cunnan/ðurfan/durran/sculan senses.

Complete present/past formation pairs for12selected lemmas; other roster citations remain audit-only. Source libbendu/flēogendu/swimmendu receive recognition with full mapped -ende pattern; participial accompaniment cweðende remains locally supplied syntax.
Full48NGDA strong/weak cells per selected model; attributive participles follow adjective choice and agreement. Distinguish predicate participles, which may be uninflected or strong-masculine-like.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
Wæs geworden in Creation is become/come-to-pass resultative close, not a transitive passive. Perfects/progressives/absolutes remain outside independent production.

Active hātan naming can take object accusative + name/predicate accusative. Ordinary periphrastic passive (ge)hāten derives from the checked participle+auxiliary rule; inherited hātte remains audit-only.
Promote eall strong NGDA and introduce image-checked longǣlc strong NGDA. Complete models do not teach unrelated indefinite pronouns, partitives, adverbial quantifier idioms or weak paradigms.
